note: Every item since Election Day, newest first, with the page it came from. Researched Nov 18 2026.

items.what: Prediction market traders give Chuck Schumer a 91 percent chance to remain Senate Democratic leader, Chris Van Hollen 8 percent and Brian Schatz 2 percent.

The AP calls Alaska's Senate race for Democrat Mary Peltola over Sen. Dan Sullivan, 50.1 to 45.8 percent, with no ranked choice count needed. Democrats flipped nine seats and hold a 56 to 44 majority.
Vice President JD Vance says he will decide whether to run for the 2028 Republican nomination sometime next year.
Fourteen Senate Democrats publicly back Schumer and four back Van Hollen. Van Hollen says at least 15 have committed to him privately.
Indivisible and National Nurses United endorse Van Hollen for majority leader, and MoveOn says 75 percent of members who voted back him.
Rep. James Comer announces a run for governor of Kentucky in 2027.
New York City DSA votes 291 to 123 for a resolution urging Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president in 2028. She has filed for reelection to the House.

A pop up super PAC, Our Heritage Matters, formed less than three weeks before Election Day and reported spending more than $8.5 million across 35 House and Senate races, in an effort to turn conservatives against Republican candidates.
Van Hollen formally challenges Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, the first contested race for the post in decades. The secret ballot vote is set for Dec 1.

Corporations gave $737.3 million to super PACs and hybrid PACs this cycle through Oct 23, 60 percent above 2024. Crypto, online betting and AI interests gave 53 percent of it, and MAGA Inc. took in the most, $141 million.

With the midterms over, the 2028 calendar takes shape: Republicans keep Iowa first, then New Hampshire, Nevada and South Carolina. Democrats left Iowa out of their early states and set penalties for candidates who campaign in unsanctioned contests.
